raw_findings.message: A direct call to `parse_row` with a three-column row indexes `row[3]` and raises `IndexError` instead of reporting a controlled malformed-row error.
Any legitimate data row whose worker field is exactly `worker` is mistaken for a header and omitted from the report.
A malformed row causes the loader to stop reading without reporting an error, so later valid rows are omitted while the command can still exit successfully.
Binary floating-point multiplication can print inaccurate billed amounts, such as `$0.30000000000000004` for three hours at a rate of 0.1.
The user-controlled output path is interpolated into a shell command, so a path containing shell metacharacters can execute arbitrary commands.
Optional duration units let empty strings and bare digits such as `8` pass validation and be counted as zero minutes.
The pattern explicitly accepts negative values, so an input such as `-2h` subtracts time from the worker's total.
The ambiguous repeated groups can cause catastrophic backtracking on a long non-matching duration, allowing an input row to consume excessive CPU and stall the report.
A worker whose entries total zero minutes causes division by zero when the report computes their overtime share.
Slicing from index 1 skips the first daily total, so overtime on a worker's first recorded day is never counted.
Saturday has weekday value 5, so the strict `> 5` condition excludes all Saturday work from weekend totals.

fixed_raw_findings.message: An empty worker field is accepted and used as an aggregation key, so rows with no worker identity are combined and reported as if they belonged to one worker.
A CSV-controlled worker name is only stripped, then emitted verbatim at line 73, so a name containing newlines or terminal control sequences can forge report entries or manipulate terminal output.

raw_findings.message: A row with fewer than four columns raises `IndexError` when this function accesses `row[3]`.
Breaking on any row-parsing exception silently discards that row and all subsequent rows while allowing the CLI to produce a partial report and exit successfully.
Using binary floating-point for billing can print inaccurate amounts, such as $0.30000000000000004 for 3 hours at a rate of 0.1.
Interpolating the user-controlled output path into a shell command allows shell metacharacters in `--out` to execute arbitrary commands.
Because the units and repeated groups are optional, malformed values such as `8` are accepted and parsed as zero minutes.
The duration pattern accepts signed values such as `-2h`, which subtract time from a worker's total and billing.
The nested repeated groups make the duration regex catastrophically backtrack on long non-matching input, allowing a crafted duration to stall parsing.
A worker with zero total minutes causes division by zero when the report computes their overtime share.
Slicing from index 1 skips the first daily total, so overtime worked on the first recorded day is never counted.
The `weekday() > 5` check excludes Saturday, so Saturday work is omitted from weekend totals.

The duration pattern accepts negative components, so input such as `-2h` subtracts time from a worker's total.

Saturday has weekday value 5, so the strict `> 5` check excludes all Saturday work from weekend totals.
